notes: Three text paragraphs occupy 26 physical typed lines. The first begins mid-word with ment; no earlier portion is supplied. There are no diagrams, drawings, displayed equations, stamps, title, date or stated total page count.
A handwritten 74 is at top centre and a lighter archive 82 at bottom left. Section 7.6.3 begins on L18. The references (7.6.1), 7.1 and 7.2 are textual references, not page counts.

The first paragraph claims finite local freeness, base-change compatibility of an underlined Hom construction, a correspondence between extensions and H_n torsors, and an equivalence under formal completion. The second claims functoriality and compatibility with maps of complete traits. These are document claims, not verified theorems in this run.

Section 7.6.3 proposes a more general noetherian adic base and calls algebraizability of the formal abelian object the essential question. It asserts that the method of 7.2 applies when S is normal. No written question mark or explicit verification reservation appears; editorial unsure marks are not manuscript questions.
Visible unusual forms retained: systêmes twice, cphérents, qutun, sbhéma, and schéma abélien par un [cancelled schéma] tore. None was repaired by grammar or by a proposed mathematical interpretation.

The mathematical setting helped locate the repeated Hom/extension group glyph and the ring corrections, but was not used to replace the oval/slash by a named group. In particular H's prose argument for Z was not treated as ink evidence.

The plain typed x in the upper H_n formula and the circle-cross tensor product in the lower G_o formula were distinguished by visible contours. All lower n indices and the rightward S-prime arrow were read directly.
The short dark line below the cancelled pe is encoded by uline inside deleted. This records its geometry without assigning an additional meaning to it.

H's introductory note and its explanatory note about the group glyph are editorial and are not transcribed as manuscript text. Their wording and an absent extraction page macro are not counted as ink discrepancies.
Manual strokes are not attributed to a named writer in this run. Inventory hand=another unnamed hand records observed handwriting without importing H's attribution.
The upper/lower round glyphs, oval/slash, low q/comma-like mark, margin V/check and original ring capital remain explicitly uncertain. The original quotient numerator has no handwritten replacement.

The recorded start time is the first clock observation after the prescribed bundle read. Each whole/half was displayed once. Ten remaining places each received one enlarged crop, displayed once; no OCR, recognition, web search, other page or other reader was used.
No proof check, independent re-proof or computation was performed; checks is deliberately empty.
